architecture.title: Two scopes, one ladder — from an observed failure to the cheapest effective component
architecture.caption: Every failure an editor can see is owned by one scope: INV (how the agent works) or DOM (what a practitioner knows). Each editor then walks the same ladder from prompts.py: skill, script, subagent, plugin, and always-on text last. A plugin needs repeated evidence that clear prose is skipped. Component choices shown are the course's SIM editors (common/h2kit.py), a teaching model of the repository's templates.

charts.title: Generic-editor ablation — score (three streams, refine half)
charts.unit: score 0–100, mean over three streams (bench.judge, after the run)
charts.caption: From Lab 03-2, SIM, captured on this Mac (library off in both loop arms). SDs 2.9–4.5. All three streams agree on both executors. The scoped-vs-generic gap is within one SD on sim-cloud (+2.7, size not shown on 17 tasks) and larger than one SD on sim-local (+4.5, a SIM assumption, not a measurement); the direction matches the paper's reported −2.9 / −3.7.
